problem: E22 empirically validated the search-existing-artifacts principle in a 3rd real domain, but whether that evidence was actually sufficient to formally promote it (vs. just "a good idea that worked 3 times") had not been judged.

decision.decision_summary: Re-verified all 3-domain provenance (exact citation, broadened to a phase's full real artifact set for E22, an honest methodological refinement); re-confirmed confidence/novelty; checked for duplication against E17's policy (none) and forced generalization (none -- reused E21's own exclusion precedent). VERDICT: ACCEPT. Promotion RECORDED (not enforced).

action.action_summary: Wrote 1 real promotion-registry record. 0 Goal/Gap/Pattern/existing-Policy modified. 0 enforcement mechanism wired in.

result.note: Records (does not enforce) a Cross-Domain Principle promotion; does not change this Goal's own real status, does not modify the Experience Layer, Pattern Registry, or E17's locked policy.

cause.root_cause_summary: A 3-domain empirical success (E22) is evidence for promotion, but promotion itself requires an explicit review step -- otherwise "it worked" silently becomes "it is now a rule" without ever being checked for duplication, forced generalization, or genuine novelty.

lesson: Promotion and enforcement are two different decisions -- recording a principle as formally recognized, while explicitly declining to wire it into any real project rule this phase, keeps the same Decision/Action separation this whole arc has relied on since E6/E13, applied here to knowledge itself rather than to code.
